label: Entity detail levels
summary: A function of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, gives the detail levels (LODs) of the shown 3D entity.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface (an entity viewer tool), not to the game's own windows. A LOD (level of detail) is a simpler version of a model used from further away. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: Has states
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the entity shown in the engine's entity viewer has states.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it. What a state is here is not documented (the game has a separate ViewerEntityState type).

label: Has unsaved changes
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the entity open in the engine's entity viewer has changes that are not saved yet.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Is looping
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the animation in the engine's entity viewer repeats when it reaches the end.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it. The same type has a ToggleLooping action.

label: Is playing
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the animation in the engine's entity viewer is playing right now.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it on this type. The music player's IsPlaying is another type and only a hint.

label: Entity name
summary: A function of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, gives the name of the shown entity.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it on this type. The game documents no return type.

label: Number of joints
summary: A whole number: going by its name, how many joints (bones of the skeleton) the entity in the engine's entity viewer has.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Pause animation
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, pauses the shown entity's animation.
details: It returns nothing. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Roll forward
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, moves forward again in its history of changes (redo).
details: It returns nothing. The same type has a Rollback action. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Roll back
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, goes back in its history of changes (undo).
details: It returns nothing. The same type has a RollForward action. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Entity scale
summary: A decimal number: going by its name, the size factor of the entity shown in the engine's entity viewer.
details: ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Viewer entity itself
summary: A function on the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, hands back the viewed entity itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types (such as Character.Self) is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set current frame
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that takes one value and, going by its name, sets the text that shows the animation's current frame.
details: It returns nothing. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it, so the exact form of the value is not shown.

label: Set current time
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that takes one value and, going by its name, sets the text that shows the animation's current time.
details: It returns nothing. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it, so the exact form of the value is not shown.

label: Entity state
summary: A function of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, gives the current state (pose or animation) of the shown entity.
details: The game has a ViewerEntityState type, but it documents no return type here and vanilla never uses it.

label: Step backwards
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, moves the animation one frame back.
details: It returns nothing. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Step forward
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, moves the animation one frame on.
details: It returns nothing. ViewerEntity belongs to the engine's internal interface; vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle looping
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, switches repeating of the animation on or off.
details: It returns nothing. The same type has an IsLooping check. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle play and pause
summary: An action of the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, plays a paused animation or pauses a playing one.
details: It returns nothing. The same type has an IsPlaying check. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Access detail level info
summary: A function on one detail level (LOD) of an entity in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, hands back that item itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Detail level number
summary: Which detail level (LOD, a simpler version of a 3D model for viewing from afar) this item describes, as a whole number.
details: The engine's entity editor shows it in its lists of a model's detail levels, as "LOD (number): (count)".

label: Number of triangles
summary: How many triangles the model has at this detail level, as a whole number.
details: The engine's entity editor shows it in its list of a model's detail levels, as "LOD (number): (triangles)".

label: Number of vertices
summary: How many vertices (corner points) the model has at this detail level, as a whole number.
details: The engine's entity editor shows it in its list of a model's detail levels, as "LOD (number): (vertices)".

label: Detail level info itself
summary: A function on one detail level (LOD) of an entity in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, hands back that item itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access entity state
summary: A function on a state of an entity in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, hands back that state itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Animation length
summary: A decimal number: going by its name, how long this state's animation lasts.
details: The unit is not documented. Belongs to the engine's internal entity viewer; vanilla never uses it.

label: Has animation
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether this state of the entity has an animation.
details: Belongs to the engine's internal entity viewer; vanilla never uses it.

label: Keyframe layers
summary: A function on a state in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, gives the keyframe layers of its animation.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: State name
summary: A function on a state in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, gives the name of that state.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; the Name lines of other types are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Number of frames
summary: A whole number: going by its name, how many frames this state's animation has.
details: Belongs to the engine's internal entity viewer; vanilla never uses it.

label: Entity state itself
summary: A function on a state in the engine's entity viewer that, going by its name, hands back that state itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access virtue or sin
summary: A function on a virtue or sin entry (a trait a faith calls virtuous or sinful) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Full description
summary: The full description text of a virtue or sin entry in the faith window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the faith window. The exact content of the text is not documented.

label: Trait
summary: The trait that this virtue or sin entry is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the faith window as the data to switch to, which shows the entry is about a trait. The game documents no return type.

label: Weight
summary: A number: going by its name, the weight of this virtue or sin entry.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; GetWeight on other windows is only a hint. What the weight affects is not documented.

label: Is sin
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether this entry is a sin of the faith.
details: The opposite of IsVirtue. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is virtue
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether this entry is a virtue of the faith.
details: The opposite of IsSin. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Virtue or sin itself
summary: A function on a virtue or sin entry that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access war
summary: A function on a war that, going by its name, hands back the war itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint. War.Self is the form vanilla uses.

label: Custom text
summary: The text a custom localization (a scripted text that picks its wording by conditions) produces for the war.
details: It takes one value: the custom localization's key in quotes, one made for wars (`type = war`). Vanilla's war declared window writes `WAR.Custom('WarDeclaredOpening')` and `WAR.Custom('WarDeclaredFlavor')` for its flavor text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Casus belli
summary: The casus belli (the reason for war, such as a claim) the war is being fought over.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to the casus belli type's icon in the interfere-in-war window, and to the defender in a contract text. The game documents no return type. The same as GetActiveCasusBelli, going by the uses.

label: Casus belli
summary: The casus belli (the reason for war) the war is being fought over.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger to show the casus belli type's icon and to reach the defender and their primary title. The game documents no return type. Going by the uses it gives the same thing as GetActiveCB.

label: Attackers
summary: The attacking side of the war.
details: It gives a WarSide (one side of the war). Vanilla switches to it in the ledger.

label: Battle results
summary: A function on a war that, going by its name, gives the results of the battles fought in it.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: War score from battles
summary: A number: going by its name, the war score (how close a side is to winning) that comes from battles.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window shows the same thing with its own WarOverviewWindow.GetBattlesWarScore, which is only a hint. Whose side the number counts for is not documented.

label: Battles war score tooltip
summary: A tooltip text that, going by its name, explains the war score from battles.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window uses its own function of the same name, which is only a hint.

label: Defenders
summary: The defending side of the war.
details: It gives a WarSide (one side of the war). Vanilla switches to it in the ledger.

label: War ID
summary: The war's ID number.
details: Vanilla passes it in the ledger to check whether the war overview of this war is the one open.

label: War score from prisoners
summary: A number: going by its name, the war score that comes from holding enemy prisoners.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window has its own function of the same name, which is only a hint.

label: Prisoners war score tooltip
summary: A tooltip text that, going by its name, explains the war score from holding prisoners.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window has its own function of the same name, which is only a hint.

label: War name
summary: The war's name as shown in the game.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as contract requests and the military view ("will stand down when the war ends").

label: War score from occupation
summary: A number: going by its name, the war score that comes from occupying enemy land.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window has its own function of the same name, which is only a hint.

label: Occupation war score tooltip
summary: A tooltip text that, going by its name, explains the war score from occupation.
details: Vanilla never uses it on War; the war overview window has its own function of the same name, which is only a hint.

label: Main enemy of the player
summary: Going by its name, the player's main opponent in the war.
details: Vanilla reaches it through WarItem.GetWar in the war icons above the map, so it does belong to the war; that use only switches to it and shows nothing more. The game documents no return type.

label: Start date
summary: The date the war began.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger to show how long the war has been going on (the time between the start date and today).

label: Ticking war score
summary: A number: the war score that comes from objectives held over time.
details: The game's own tooltip header calls this war score from held objectives. Vanilla shows a part of the ledger only when it is above 0. Whose side it counts for is not documented.

label: Ticking war score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score from held objectives.
details: Vanilla puts it under a header in the ledger's held-objective tooltip.

label: War score
summary: A number: the war's current war score (how close a side is to winning).
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger as a bar and as a number with a plus or minus sign, so it can be negative.

label: War score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war's current war score.
details: Vanilla uses it on the war score in the ledger.

label: Is valid
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the war is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger and the military window as a condition for showing parts, so they appear only when it is true. What makes a war invalid is not documented.

label: War as script scope
summary: The war turned into a script scope, so script values, variables and the like can be read from it in a text.
details: Vanilla uses it in contract texts as War.MakeScope().ScriptValue(...) to compare a script value of the war.

label: War itself
summary: The war itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it in the ledger to open the war overview of this war. The game documents no return type.

label: Access war ally
summary: A function on a war ally entry that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Reason for joining
summary: The text that says why this ally joins the war.
details: Vanilla shows it under the ally's name in the tooltip of a defender's ally.

label: Ally
summary: The character of this war ally entry.
details: Vanilla switches to it in the declare war window to show the ally. The game documents no return type.

label: War ally itself
summary: A function on a war ally entry that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access war declared window
summary: A function on the war declared window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: The war declared window pops up when a war is declared. Vanilla never names AccessSelf on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the war declared window.
details: Vanilla puts it on the window's close buttons.

label: Attackers
summary: The list of attackers shown in the war declared window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list (datamodel) behind the attackers' entries. The game documents no return type.

label: Flavor text
summary: The flavor text (a short story line) of the war declared window.

label: Main attacker
summary: The main attacker of the newly declared war.
details: Vanilla switches to it in the war declared window. The game documents no return type.

label: Military strength
summary: The military strength comparison of the two sides, shown in the war declared window.
details: It gives a GuiMilitaryStrength (the interface's strength comparison). Vanilla switches to it in the window.

label: War
summary: The war that the war declared window is about.
details: Vanilla shows the war's name from it. The game documents no return type.

label: Open war view
summary: An action of the war declared window that, going by its name, opens the full view of the war.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: War declared window itself
summary: A function on the war declared window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Attacker AI war coordinator
summary: The AI war coordinator (the AI's war planning) of the attacking side, for the debug watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the debug AI war coordinator watch window, a developer tool. The game documents no return type.

label: Defender AI war coordinator
summary: The AI war coordinator (the AI's war planning) of the defending side, for the debug watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the debug AI war coordinator watch window, a developer tool. The game documents no return type.

label: Access war info
summary: A function on a war entry of the debug AI war coordinator window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: War
summary: The war this entry of the debug AI war coordinator window is about.
details: Vanilla shows the war's name from it. The game documents no return type.

label: Is collapsed
summary: Yes or no: whether this war's entry in the debug AI war coordinator window is folded shut.
details: Vanilla shows the entry's details only when it is not collapsed; ToggleCollapsed switches it.

label: War info itself
summary: A function on a war entry of the debug AI war coordinator window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Fold or unfold
summary: Folds this war's entry in the debug AI war coordinator window shut, or opens it again.
details: Vanilla puts it on the entry's expand and collapse buttons; IsCollapsed tells the current state.

label: Access war icon
summary: A function on a war icon above the map that, going by its name, hands back the item itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Can enforce victory
summary: Yes or no: whether the player can force victory in this war now.
details: Vanilla uses it on the war icons above the map (in hud.gui) to show an orange glow and the war-won icon when it is true.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a war icon above the map.

label: War
summary: The war that this war icon above the map stands for.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to the player's main enemy. The game documents no return type.

label: War score share
summary: A number: the war score of this war as a fraction, shown on the war icon as a percentage with a sign.
details: Vanilla formats it as a percent with plus or minus, so it can be negative.

label: Is player in war
summary: Yes or no: whether the player takes part in the war of this war icon.
details: Vanilla shows different parts of the icon depending on it.

label: Click war icon
summary: What happens when the war icon above the map is clicked.
details: Vanilla puts it on the icon's onclick; what the click opens is not documented.

label: War icon itself
summary: A function on a war icon above the map that, going by its name, hands back the item itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access war overview
summary: A function on the war overview window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Can send
summary: Yes or no: whether the peace or victory proposal in the war overview window can be sent now.
details: Vanilla enables the send button only when it is true.

label: Can demand victory
summary: Yes or no: whether a victory demand can be sent in the war overview window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a glow effect on the send button.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the war overview window.

label: Close peace terms
summary: An action of the war overview window that, going by its name, closes the peace terms panel.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it; IsPeaceTermsOpen tells whether the panel is open.

label: Allows hostages
summary: Yes or no: whether hostages can be used to settle this war.
details: Vanilla shows the hostage exchange part of the peace terms only when it is true, and otherwise a text that hostages cannot be used for this casus belli. It shows different hostage parts for landless adventurers.

label: Expected answer
summary: The text of the other side's expected answer to the proposed peace terms.
details: Vanilla shows it on the acceptance bar above the send button, when the player takes part and an answer is needed.

label: Answer reasons
summary: The tooltip text with the reasons behind the other side's expected answer to the peace terms.
details: Vanilla puts it on the acceptance bar.

label: Acceptance chance
summary: A decimal number: how likely the other side is to accept the proposed peace terms, shown as a bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of the acceptance progress bar.

label: War score from battles
summary: The war score from battles, as ready text for the war overview window.
details: It returns text, unlike War.GetBattlesWarScore, which gives a number.

label: Battles war score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score from battles in the war overview window.

label: Beneficiary name
summary: The name of the player's beneficiary in this war (the one who gets the gains).
details: Vanilla shows it under the heading "Your beneficiary".

label: Contribution rank
summary: A whole number: the given character's rank among the war's participants by contribution.
details: It takes the character as its one value; vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) and shows the rank as an ordinal (1st, 2nd …). Vanilla shows a different text when the rank is 0, which seems to mean no rank.

label: Effects description
summary: The text that lists the further effects of ending the war the way the selected tab says (defeat, white peace or victory).
details: Vanilla shows it in the peace terms panel below the main outcome.

label: Effects label
summary: A text that, going by its name, labels the effects of the selected peace terms tab.
details: Vanilla never uses it on the war overview window; the declare war window's function of the same name is only a hint.

label: Main outcome
summary: The text with the main outcome of ending the war the way the selected tab says.
details: Vanilla shows it at the top of the peace terms panel, highlighted.

label: Hostage exchange
summary: The hostage exchange part of the war overview window.
details: Vanilla switches to it for the hostage parts of the peace terms. The game documents no return type.

label: War score from prisoners
summary: The war score from holding prisoners, as ready text for the war overview window.

label: Prisoners war score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score from holding prisoners in the war overview window.

label: Left side
summary: The war side shown on the left of the war overview window.
details: It gives a WarSide. The game documents nothing about which side (attackers or defenders) is on the left; the same window has IsLeftSideAttacker.

label: Left allies heading
summary: The heading text over the allies of the left side in the war overview window.

label: Left army makeup
summary: The army composition of the left side in the war overview window.
details: It gives an ArmyComposition.

label: Left side heading
summary: The heading text of the left side in the war overview window.

label: Left side leader
summary: The entry of the left side's leader in the war overview window.
details: It gives a WarParticipantItem. Vanilla also asks it whether the leader is the attacker, to pick the stance name.

label: Left main participant
summary: Going by its name, an entry of a main participant on the left side, chosen by its one value.
details: It gives a WarParticipantItem. Vanilla never uses it on this window; the battle and combat windows' functions of the same name are only a hint, and what the value stands for is not documented.

label: Left main participants
summary: The list of the main participants of the left side in the war overview window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list (datamodel). The game documents no return type.

label: Left allies
summary: The list of the allies on the left side in the war overview window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list and also counts it for the allies heading.

label: Military strength
summary: The military strength comparison of the two sides in the war overview window.
details: It gives a GuiMilitaryStrength.

label: War score from occupation
summary: The war score from occupying land, as ready text for the war overview window.

label: Occupation war score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score from occupation in the war overview window.

label: Player
summary: The player character, as seen by the war overview window.
details: Vanilla checks the player's government with it, to show the right hostage parts for landless adventurers.

label: Player's entry
summary: The player's own participant entry in the war overview window.
details: It gives a WarParticipantItem.

label: War score bar value
summary: A decimal number: the war score as a position on the war overview's war score bar.
details: Vanilla fills the bar out of 100, treats 50 as the middle, and changes the bar's look below 25 and above 75. Which side the high end belongs to is not documented.

label: Right side
summary: The war side shown on the right of the war overview window.
details: It gives a WarSide.

label: Right allies heading
summary: The heading text over the allies of the right side in the war overview window.

label: Right army makeup
summary: The army composition of the right side in the war overview window.
details: It gives an ArmyComposition.

label: Right side heading
summary: The heading text of the right side in the war overview window.

label: Right side leader
summary: The entry of the right side's leader in the war overview window.
details: It gives a WarParticipantItem. Vanilla also compares the leader's faith with the player's.

label: Right main participant
summary: Going by its name, an entry of a main participant on the right side, chosen by its one value.
details: It gives a WarParticipantItem. Vanilla never uses it on this window; the battle and combat windows' functions of the same name are only a hint, and what the value stands for is not documented.

label: Right main participants
summary: The list of the main participants of the right side in the war overview window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list (datamodel). The game documents no return type.

label: Right allies
summary: The list of the allies on the right side in the war overview window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list and also counts it for the allies heading.

label: Send button text
summary: The text on the send button of the war overview's peace terms.

label: Send button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the send button of the war overview's peace terms.

label: Ticking war score
summary: The war score that builds up over time, as ready text for the war overview window.

label: Ticking war score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score building up over time in the war overview window.

label: War
summary: The war the war overview window shows.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to the start date and to the casus belli (for example whether a white peace is possible). The game documents no return type.

label: War duration
summary: The text with how long ago the war started.
details: Vanilla uses it in "War Started: ... ago".

label: War score
summary: The war's current war score, as ready text for the war overview window.

label: War score tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the war score in the war overview window.

label: War stance description
summary: The description of a side's stance in the war, for a tooltip.
details: Its one value is yes or no for whether the side is the attacker; vanilla passes the side leader's IsAttacker.

label: War stance name
summary: The name of a side's stance in the war.
details: Its one value is yes or no for whether the side is the attacker; vanilla passes the side leader's IsAttacker.

label: Battles score capped
summary: Yes or no: whether the war score from battles has reached its maximum.
details: Vanilla then shows a short "Max!" note (text key BATTLES_WAR_SCORE_CAPPED) next to the battles war score.

label: Defeat tab selected
summary: Yes or no: whether the defeat tab of the peace terms is selected.
details: Vanilla shows the tab button pressed when it is true and hides a further part of the peace terms on that tab. The same window has SetEffectsTabDefeat.

label: Victory tab selected
summary: Yes or no: whether the victory tab of the peace terms is selected.
details: Vanilla shows the tab button pressed when it is true. The same window has SetEffectsTabVictory.

label: White peace tab selected
summary: Yes or no: whether the white peace tab (ending the war without a winner) of the peace terms is selected.
details: Vanilla shows the tab button pressed when it is true. The same window has SetEffectsTabWhitePeace.

label: Is great holy war
summary: Yes or no: whether the war shown is a great holy war (a crusade or similar).
details: Vanilla shows different parts of the window for great holy wars.

label: Left side attacks
summary: Yes or no: whether the left side of the war overview window is the attacking side.

label: Peace terms open
summary: Yes or no: whether the peace terms panel of the war overview window is open.
details: Vanilla shows the war end terms panel only when it is true.

label: Is player involved
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the player is involved in the war shown.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it uses IsPlayerParticipant instead. How the two differ is not documented.

label: Is player in war
summary: Yes or no: whether the player takes part in the war shown.
details: Vanilla shows the send button only then, and the acceptance bar when an answer is also needed.
